name: Kayla Harrison
summary: The UFC women's bantamweight champion (19-1, age 36): two-time Olympic judo gold medallist and two-time PFL champion. She won the title by kimura over Julianna Peña in June 2025 and has not fought since. Neck surgery for herniated discs forced her out of the January date with Amanda Nunes. She says she feels 'awesome' now. The cut to 135 is a known strain on her.

how_they_fight.Striking: Functional, used mainly to get to the clinch. Six KO/TKO wins, all in the PFL or Invicta; four came in R1. Opponents have landed little on her in the UFC: Holm 2, Vieira 24, Peña 9 significant strikes (our data).
how_they_fight.Grappling: Elite. Body-lock takedowns into top control and submissions. Against Peña she took her down with a body lock in each round and finished with a kimura from side control at 4:55 of R2 (Cageside). Eight submission wins. In three UFC fights she held top position for about 5, 8 and 6 minutes.
how_they_fight.Defense: Her one loss was a five-round decision to Larissa Pacheco in 2022. She has never been finished.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Fourteen stoppages: nine in R1, four in R2, one in R3. She is 1-1 in five-round fights, both against Pacheco. The weight cut is a recurring concern: she was hospitalised the week before UFC 307 after seeing blood in her urine, and said she is 'just not built to weigh 135 pounds' (LowKick).
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Conservative and control-first. After Vieira she said it 'definitely wasn't my best night'. She has said she could walk away from the sport now and be at peace (Uncrowned).

patterns: Body lock, trip, top control, submission
Front-loaded finisher: 13 of 14 stoppages in R1-R2
Wins rounds through control time even when she can't finish (Vieira)
concerns: About 17 months out of the cage
Neck surgery: five herniated discs, eight weeks in a neck brace, and two discs still to address after her career (Uncrowned)
Only one five-round win, and she lost the other
keys_to_beat: Defend the body lock and keep the fight at range
Make her work late in a five-round fight

news.text: Says she questioned whether she would feel like herself again after neck surgery, but 'I'm back' and feels 'awesome'.
Told Uncrowned she probably would not have come back if Nunes had not returned from retirement.
Joselyne Edwards is the backup for the title fight.
